title: Choose the visual world
question: Multi-session research desk for a resume-grade demo: architecture + report + metrics. Keep the assigned world, take a fused alternate, re-roll, or play the category standard.

options.label: Stage tape desk
options.lineage: orchestration timeline / stage Gantt + multi-session research desk
options.body: The product is a desk where a research job unrolls as a horizontal stage tape: plan → parallel research lanes → normalize → verify (pass/revise) → final. Sessions live on a rail; a metrics strip shows resume-friendly numbers (wall time, stage count, fan-out N, verdict/retry, synthetic tokens/cost labeled DEMO). Cool lab-gray surfaces, one restrained signal accent, tabular digits for instruments. First viewport: session archive + empty compose with dormant tape and zeroed instruments—run animates the tape and fills the report. Risk: if metrics and report are weak, it reads as project-management chrome.

options.label: Event reconstruction
options.lineage: particle-detector event display × multi-agent research job
options.body: One research job is one frozen collision event. Sub-questions are tracks through concentric detector layers (pipeline stages); deposited-energy bars become DEMO metrics; sessions are an event browser. Near-black vacuum ground, steel-blue rings, signal yellow/cyan tracks. Strongest “show the architecture” read for technical interviews. Risk: sci-fi density can overshadow the final report unless the report is a first-class panel after reconstruction.

options.label: Eval test bench
options.lineage: lab test bench: adjust · launch · trace through a measured field
options.body: Adjust the query, launch a simulated job, watch the trajectory through stages while instruments update. Resume numbers are native (latency, cost, coverage properties, pass/revise). Neutral bench materials, high-contrast readouts, clear launch control. Risk: without a bold stage graph, it can look like generic MLOps SaaS.
